title: Provisional Cutover Protocol for Reserved Quota Rollovers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines and implements a provisional cutover protocol for reserved-capacity quota rollovers to eliminate transient double-counting and lost-credits during tenant transfers, timezone migrations, and late-arriving usage events. We aim to make daily/monthly/rolling-window resets deterministic and observable while minimizing customer-visible errors during reserved pool migrations and billing boundary changes.

Problem statement:
- Customers in Reserved (committed) capacity occasionally observe incorrect quota balances immediately after cutovers (migration between pools, billing boundary change, or tenant timezone adjustments). Root causes include: race conditions between ledger reset and late ingestion, partial replication lag across regions, and non-atomic tenant transfer procedures.
- Existing heuristics (soft-guard and backfill runs) reduce impact but are slow and sometimes trigger transient overage enforcement or unexpected throttles.

Goals:
1) Ensure no tenant loses more than 1% of its reserved tokens during cutover operations (measured across a 24h window).
2) Avoid transient double-counting that could cause immediate overage blocking.
3) Provide clear, actionable telemetry and an automated short-window reconciliation that can be triggered post-cutover.
4) Keep the protocol lightweight and compatible with both hosted and dedicated deployments (including Private).

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: cutovers that involve quota reset boundaries (daily/monthly/rolling) and reserved pool transfers for tenant-level moves. Includes UTC-anchored resets and tenant timezone migrations where anchor changes.
- Non-goal: rewriting global billing ledger architecture. This is an add-on protocol with clear handshakes and temporary shadow ledgers to ensure safe transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Automated cutover handshake implemented between quota service and reservation manager with idempotent message semantics (at-least-once safe).
Post-cutover reconciliation job runs within 5 minutes and converges ledger to expected state for 99.9% of test tenants in staging.
Integration tests cover late-arriving events up to 15 minutes and ensure no more than 0.5% of tokens are misaccounted per tenant.
Cutover telemetry dashboard surfaces per-tenant drift, reconciliation time, and any auto-adjustments; alerts when drift >1% for any tenant.
Procedures and runbook updated and approved by oncall and billing ownership.
design_notes: High level approach: introduce a provisional cutover protocol that uses a short-lived shadow ledger and an atomic lease handshake. On cutover, writes go to both primary and shadow ledgers while reads for enforcement use a conservative min(primary, shadow-projection) to avoid double-counting. A background consolidator reconciles deltas and makes a single commit when safe.

Key components:
- Cutover Coordinator: initiates handshakes and issues cutover tokens.
- Shadow Ledger: per-tenant ephemeral ledger storing deltas for the transition window.
- Consolidator: idempotent job that reconciles shadow -> primary and emits refunds/credits if under-count detected.
- Lease/Checkpoint: short-lived cutover lease to prevent concurrent cutovers for same tenant.

Trade-offs considered:
- Performance vs correctness: writing to two ledgers increases write RT cost slightly (~5-8% P95 write latency). We prefer correctness for cutover windows.
- Complexity vs coverage: limited to reserved pool/tz-migration/cutover flows instead of all quota changes to reduce blast radius.
- Backfill window: default 15 minutes (configurable); longer windows increase reconciliation work and cost.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API + handshake): Add Cutover Coordinator API. Implement lease acquisition and cutover token issuance. Integrate with reservation-manager to detect tenant-transfer and timezone-change events. (Owners: Liam, Priya)

Phase 2 (Shadow ledger): Implement lightweight shadow ledger backed by existing ledger storage namespace; shadow writes are labeled and TTLed. Ensure write path is idempotent and measurable. (Owners: Marco, Jamila)

Phase 3 (Read-mode enforcement): Modify enforcement layer to consult conservative projection during active cutover: enforced_remaining = min(primary_remaining, projected_primary_from_shadow). This prevents both under- and over-enforcement. (Owners: Quentin)

Phase 4 (Consolidator and telemetry): Build idempotent reconciler job that runs continuously for active cutovers and a one-off converge endpoint. Emit metrics: cutover_start_ts, consolidator_duration_ms, tokens_reconciled, drift_pct. (Owners: Nikhil)

Phase 5 (Staging validation & long-running tests): End-to-end tests that simulate: partial replication, 2-region writes, 10k tenants cutover, late events up to 15 minutes. Validate SLOs and update runbooks. (Owners: QA)
Phase 6 (Gradual rollout): Canary on dedicated -> 10% reserved customers -> 100%. Monitor telemetry and have rollback triggers. (Owners: Oncall, Product Ops)
migration_plan: Migration for existing tenants is opt-in per tenant during scheduled maintenance windows. Default behavior remains unchanged until tenant cutover is requested.
Before cutover: schedule conversation with account team, snapshot tenant ledger, and run dry-run in staging.
During cutover: acquire lease, enable shadow ledger for tenant, and begin concurrent writes for pre-configured window.

After cutover: run consolidator. If drift <= configured threshold, commit final ledger and delete shadow. If drift > alert threshold, escalate to engineering/billing-runbook and hold final commit until manual review.
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: cutover.active_count, cutover.start_duration_ms, cutover.consolidation_time_ms, cutover.drift_tokens, cutover.drift_pct_per_tenant, cutover.auto_adjustments_count
Dashboards: per-release and per-tenant view showing pre/post balances, reconciler progress, and recent late events. Include a histogram of late-event arrival times to tune default window.
Alerts: page on any tenant with drift_pct > 1.0% after consolidation OR if consolidator job fails > 3 consecutive times. Warning alert at drift_pct > 0.5%.
Logging: structured logs for lease acquisition, shadow-write ids, and consolidator commits with trace ids to correlate with request flows.
rollout_plan: Canary: enable protocol for internal staging tenants and 2 non-critical dedicated customers. Run for 48h and evaluate drift metrics.
Phase roll: open to selected reserved customers via opt-in flag and instrument additional telemetry. Monitor for 7 days.
GA: default enabled for all tenant transfers once metrics meet thresholds for 72h across canary and phase cohorts. Provide customer-facing docs and support scripts.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial scoping and goals added. Confirmed target drift thresholds with billing PM (Sofia).
2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Implemented prototype Cutover Coordinator API in sandbox. Observed ~6% P95 write latency increase when shadow enabled in microbenchmarks. Marking performance beta.
2026-03-05 - Marco: Shadow ledger storage implemented; TTL and compaction strategy discussed. We'll reuse ledger namespace and add a 'cutover' tag to minimize infra changes.
2026-03-06 - Priya (PM): Reviewed and approved the opt-in migration flow. Requesting clearer customer communication for expected maintenance window.

2026-03-07 - Quentin (Eng Reviewer): Critical feedback: enforcement min(primary, projection) may be too conservative for high-utilization tenants and could cause inadvertent throttling. Suggest fallback policy: if both values diverge > 2% and tenant SLA tier is enterprise, consult historical utilization model to choose enforcement value.

2026-03-08 - Liam Chen: Addressed Quentin's concern by adding a fallback consult to the utilization model; updated enforcement implementation to include SLA-tier override. Added unit tests for enforcement policy.
2026-03-09 - Nikhil: Consolidator idempotency work completed; reconciliation job emits trace id and token-delta metrics. Beginning staging runs.

2026-03-10 - QA: Found edge-case where late events arriving >15 minutes cause drift >1% for very large token-consuming tenants. Recommendation: increase default window to 30 minutes for these tenants or require pre-cutover quiesce. Adding follow-up ticket to handle exception.
